newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE ends lower amid election, rates jitters.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE ends lower amid election, rates jitters.

text.p: The UK stock market hit its lowest level in six weeks on Tuesday, as weak futures prices and worries about interest rates and the U.S. elections hit prices.

The FTSE 100 index of leading shares ended the day at 3,921.1 points, down 7.0 points on the day and just 10 points off the day's low, as investors ignored firm gilts, a solid start on Wall Street and strong performances from bourses across much of Europe.

Fears that President Bill Clinton's Democrats could wrest power from the Republicans in Congress and launch a wave of tax and spend policies weighed on sentiment in Britain despite Wall Street's increasing belief the Republicans would hold their own.
